text: The spread of AR technology is limited, yet there are some interesting approaches to investigate the impact ofvisualized AI assistants on humans. Krop et al. used 2D embodied IVAs and show that both a human-likeappearance of the assistant and framing the expertise of an agent impact the trust, acceptance, perceivedwarmth and competence perceived by the user [2]. They state that using 2D instead of 3D limits the feelingof realism and therefore affect the results. Other research also indicates that social presence in AR has aspositive influence on the users preferences, although this effect seems to be limited [8].Secondly, there is some research that examines the relationship and way of interaction between humans andnon-visualized IVAs. Lee et al. explored the interaction with voice assistants mimicking different social rolesin both functional and social tasks [3]. They point out a correlation between the different roles of the IVA andthe humans feeling of faith, trust and comfort into it. It also seems that the humans trust in differs betweenthe variable types of tasks.
